thread:
ara: Heads-up — seeing steady RSS growth from the KV cache on long-context inference (50k+ tokens). Not an immediate OOM, but fragmentation metric keeps climbing and perf slowly regresses over ~1h runs.

ara: Attaching a couple quick diagnostics I pulled from a repro:
```
KVCache summary:
  total_alloc: 19.3GB
  in_use: 12.7GB
  free_frag: 2.8GB
  slabs: 127
  avg_block: 64KB
  compaction_runs: 2
  last_compact: 2025-09-18T14:12:07Z
```

ops-bot: :warning: alert: kv_cache_fragmentation high (service=runtime-hosted-prod). Not triggering autoscale but increased tail latency observed.

miguel: Thanks for the callout. Two quick notes: (1) our allocator uses power-of-two bucket sizing so with avg block ~64KB we likely have internal slack for many short KV entries. (2) compaction happens on eviction now and is O(n) in slab count — works but spikes CPU and doesn't fully coalesce small fragments.

miguel: Proposal: trial a smaller base block (32KB) + adaptive compaction policy. Hypothesis: smaller block reduces internal slack for short-lived KV entries, reducing free_frag; adaptive compaction avoids sweeping on every eviction.

sasha: Ran a quick micro-bench on a 50k-token synthetic trace (8 concurrent sessions) with the repro harness. Results:
```
baseline (64KB): RSS=21.1GB free_frag=2.8GB p50=24ms p99=110ms
32KB block: RSS=17.3GB free_frag=0.9GB p50=25ms p99=125ms
notes: ~18% RSS drop, fragmentation down a lot, p99 +15ms (likely CPU on smaller allocations)
```

devin: Nice numbers. A few tradeoffs to think about: more blocks => more metadata and more frequent compaction windows. We should try async background compaction (compaction threads that coalesce when CPU slack is detected) vs foreground compaction on eviction. Pseudocode:
```
if (free_frag_ratio > THRESHOLD && cpu_idle > MIN_IDLE)
  schedule_background_compact();
else if (eviction_needed && free_frag_ratio > HARD_LIMIT)
  do_foreground_compact();
```

miguel: Agree. Also try a hybrid allocator: keep large-block pools for very long KV pages (full-context caches) and small-block pools for short prefixes. We can tune boundary by entry lifetime stats (hot vs cold).

ara: +1 on hybrid. Can we add instrumentation to the runtime to tag allocations with "expected_ttl" (based on context-length and token age) so the allocator can place them into appropriate pools? That would avoid one-size-fits-all.

sasha: I pushed a tiny benchmark harness change (repro/kv_probe) to log allocation lifetimes. Early peek shows ~60% of blocks are <10ms lifetime in our long-context workload (they're churn from prefix reuse). I'll open the perf numbers in a shared gist.

emily: From rollout perspective we should: 1) run these configs in dedicated-canary for 24h across varying batch sizes, 2) compare cost per token and tail latency, 3) monitor error budgets. Who wants to own the canary job?

miguel: I can own the test infra and iterate on block sizes (64KB, 48KB, 32KB) + compaction policy (evict-foreground, periodic-bg). I'll create a job matrix.

devin: For compaction algorithm, consider also incremental compaction (compact only neighboring small fragments if they cross page boundary) to avoid full-scan. Implementation sketch: maintain free-list sorted by address and try buddy-merge heuristics on allocation windows.

ara: Good. Action items:
- miguel: create canary job matrix + initial PR for allocator config flags (block_size_hint, compact_mode).
- sasha: add allocation-lifetime tagging and upload the gist of distribution.
- devin: draft async compaction patch (non-blocking).
- emily: schedule canary and add dashboards for free_frag, rss, p99 latency, cpu% during compaction.

ara: One more thing — we should gate any aggressive compaction behind a feature flag (runtime.kv.compact_mode) and keep the old path for rollback. No risky change in hosted autopilot without fallbacks.

sasha: quick note — lowering block size to 32KB gave better memory but increased fragmentation of metadata region (we saw more cache misses). Need to measure kernel scheduler impact on p99.

miguel: I'll start a PR tomorrow with flags + CI microbench. Planning to run canary next Tue for 24h.

ara: Awesome. If someone can add a short doc blurb on expected tradeoffs (RSS vs CPU vs tail latency) I'll post it to #eng-runtime and ops. :thumbsup:

emily: I'll take the doc + dashboards. Thanks team.

ops-bot: Deploy job queued: infra/canary/kv-allocator-experiment (owner=miguel). Will report back when finished.
